props.text: good morning and welcome dear medical students congratulations on making it to medical school this is an exciting day that will hopefully be always remembered as a happy memory my name is ahmed al-shashay i will be joining you on a trip to discover what it means to be a physician and what are the qualities that are expected of a professional doctor the goal of today's lecture is to make you familiar with the term professionalism and what we mean by professionalism in this subject the learning objectives are to understand the term medical professionalism and identify its connotation and meaning to learn about the scope of the subject and different concepts involved in professional character or physician and to receive an overview of the course including general outlines the lectures you are going to take this year and the assessment plan first we need to define professionalism the word professionalism professionalism is defined as the competence or skill expected of a professional so someone who practices a certain profession should have certain qualities and should have certain skills about him now what do you think is or what do you think are the the qualities and skills that are required for from someone who practices the profession of medicine the american board of internal medicine says that aspiring toward altruism accountability excellence duty service honor integrity and respect for others these are the qualities and skills that are requested or that are expected of a physician to be able to perform his job again to aspire towards altruism accountability excellence duty service honor integrity and respect for others along the course we are going to examine these terms in a more close manner we are going to dissect them and see how to perform these actions as second nature in our practice i would now like you to go to nearpod.com from your browser and enter this code into the field in front of you the feed that's pointed out in the lecture and try to brainstorm and think about what qualities you think should a physician have dealing with a patient just imagine yourself in this situation you are dealing with a patient or maybe even better imagine that you are a patient and that you are going to a physician what qualities do you think that you would expect in that physician what skills do you want this physician to have we do not live in this world alone we live with other people and to be able to perform our profession among these people and for them there is a social contract that we have made with society this social contract represents two sides what society expects from doctors and physicians and what doctors and physicians expect from society on the one hand society's expectations of medicine are to perform our service as healers this is our prime objective to heal people to society needs to be assured that we are doing our best to remain competent to have the best the best knowledge and the best practice that help us perform our function as healers to do our service altruistically not thinking of ourselves or of our benefits or whatever financial benefits i may gain or social benefits or reputation but to think of my patients best interest to have morality and integrity and to be guided by the morals of medicine that we are going to discuss in medical ethics to be accountable for whatever i do to be able to stand up for if i make a mistake to be able to stand up and defend myself and defend my profession to be transparent not to hide anything from my patients to give objective advice to the best interest of my patient and to promote public goods on the other hand medicine has requirements or has expectations from society and these are trust we need people to trust us to be able to perform our profession autonomy we need to be autonomous in our decisions and we need to have autonomy in our practice self-regulation we need to regulate our own business not have anyone else regulate our practice for us to be able to work in a health care system that is value driven and adequately funded of course it goes without saying that the funding of the health care system does not come from doctors or physicians it comes from society from taxpayers even if out of pocket if patients pay out of pocket you you're still funding the healthcare system you're working with with the money of other people and that is what you expect from them to fund your practice participation in public policy the very clear example was the very near future the covet epidemic a pandemic where public policy was dictated by physicians shared responsibility for health we would like to share in the responsibility of the health of society we do not like to be excluded from something like this we need a monopoly on our practice and here monopoly means that we need to be sure that no one practices medicine other than qualified personnel today you have started your trip to become a qualified person to practice medicine this is something that should be assured and that is practiced frequently anyone who practices medicine outside the medical profession is punished and should be banned from doing this and of course at the end it is an expectation from society for a doctor to have non-financial and financial rewards in the middle between these two fields or between these two expectations lies the good medical practice where doctors can provide service to the society and society provides doctors with the means to perform their profession having the qualities we discussed in the last slide and assuring society of that we are fulfilling the our side of the social contract is not enough to be to be done in reality but without conveying this message to patients and to society if society if you if you perform your actions with altruism but society does not see that you are performing it with altruism but your patient does not perceive that you are altruistic in this situation you have lost a lot of benefit imagine a situation where you are doing the best for your patient but your patient on the other hand thinks that you are doing this for your own benefit for your own financial benefit for example their trust in your service is going to be lost and therefore their value of the healthcare service that they are getting is going to diminish considerably the problem with reality and appearance is first of all there is an abundance of information today on the internet in our front pockets on our mobile phones anyone can find information anywhere even us doctors when we try to look for information we look for it on our phones and on our laptops and browser screens this is also available to all people people who look for information think why do i need a doctor now i have all the information on the internet if they trust their physicians if they trust the healthcare system they are working with they are going to understand that there is a higher value with our physicians the other problem is the infodemic this is a term that was coined recently to describe misinformation and disinformation misinformation is information that is just plain wrong it's someone who thought about something they just put it out there on the internet and they think it is right people believe it sometimes when it actually has no base effect on the other hand this information is information wrong information that is placed on the internet and that is placed in the world on purpose of being wrong it is information that is meant for someone to sell something or to [Music] market something market a product that is not beneficial and for that reason they have to forge some information and place it into the minds of people and that is why it is important for us to have transparency and to have proper sources for our information and to convey this to the public and of course today with the social uh network and with uh with associate with the influence of the social network the public sentiment is a very big problem people can be roused up against some issue or some person with with very much ease so this is why with public sentiment we need to be careful and we need to be uh to project our transparency and our altruism in a better way and finally we need to advocate our business of course this is a less known uh hollywood actor he only recently had his oscar and he is most known for his advocacy for environmental issues this means that he goes about every practice that he has he goes about every situation or every meeting that he has and he advocates actions and he advocates the good of nature and good of the environment this is what we should be doing for our medical profession we need to be advocates for our medical profession and to be advocates you need to bear in mind it's not only enough for me to be a professional and to have the qualities and skills of a professional but i need to project that onto everyone who talks to me i need to have the appearance of being a professional as well as the reality of being a professional within myself the scope of this subject consists of four main topics four main headers first is good medical practice the second is medical ethics the third is communication skills and the fourth is we will only touch on quality at the end of the course good medical practice is a phrase that makes explicit and clear the standards of professional conduct expected of doctors by their professional peers in the community good medical practice is the manual of the competencies and skills that we described before so in traditional medicine what you learn is information about drugs disease about bacteria about trauma you you learn about the disease and you learn about the treatment but in to be able to use the this this information that you have about disease and about treatment you need to deal with real people and in dealing with these people you are controlling their lives and you have as we said before to project yourself in a certain way to be able to communicate with them in a certain way and this is what good medical practice contains medical ethics is an applied branch of the philosophy of ethics that analyzes the practice of clinical medicine and related scientific research we are going to talk in length about the medical ethics and about the concepts of medical ethics which has been debated for many years and since even antiquity but there are certain very clear rules about medical ethics that we are going to discuss we are going to see that you have to observe these rules in every encounter that you make with your patients it is very important to communicate what you want with people and in a lot of in a lot of situations this is not as easy as it sounds you need to be able to communicate something with someone that does not understand your terms to be able to communicate important information and stress on its importance and to be able to listen to other people and to understand their complaints and to understand what is valuable for them this is very important for a physician to have and finally in quality we are going to have a quick overview of how it is how we can be able to make sure that all activities are carried out the right manner the first time and every time this is the definition of quality again we are going to quickly brush over the concepts of quality at the end of the course but we are going to nonetheless uh try and understand the concept of quality and what it entails uh the institute of medicine defines six domains to measure and describe quality of care in health which are safety effectiveness to be patient-centered to be timely to be able to perform the service in good time to be efficient with no waste and to be equitable to be accessible by all people again we are going to touch on every one of these fields along the course now you may think after hearing this lecture that when who doesn't act like this who doesn't act with good medical practice in mind who doesn't act ethically or who does not act uh communicate well with their patients believe it or not in a lot of situations these rules are completely discarded they are done without and it's not always um by mistake or through omission but sometimes it is even done on purpose and that is why a lot of doctors and this is one activity that you can do is go to other doctors and ask them about good medical practice about medical ethics and about how they struggle sometimes with situations to be able to act in these ways so one good example for good medical practice is the role as leader of the medical team this is one conflict that always arises in medical teams a physician regards himself as a leader of the team and therefore he has less regard and less respect for the role of other contributors to this team uh a doctor may act uh in in in a utilitarian way he may act with uh only his opinion on the table he disregards the opinion of others like nursing staff like technical staff like even the patient sometimes so this is absolutely wrong ethical practice again doctor's personal views come into play here and the doctor's superior knowledge sometimes one of the important principles of ethics is autonomy we are going to discuss this at length in the next lecture um doctors usually disregard autonomy completely and think that they know what is best for their patients and therefore they have to um to decide and to enforce their knowledge even through coercion sometimes good communication a lot of doctors think because i am pressed for time i don't have time to communicate everything clearly to my patient i don't have time to listen to my patient i have to be very quick in my interview and therefore i don't need good communication how many times have you visited the doctor and thought well he didn't listen to me very well or i didn't really understand what he said and finally quality practice and quality if you ask any politician that you know they will tell you that it is a very difficult task to get the medical staff on board to perform quality uh actions or to perform their their practice with quality standards again this is sometimes because of scarce resources this is sometimes because of financial gain if i perform with quality i'm going to have less production and therefore i'm going to make less money can you think of any examples for these arguments can you think of any more examples for these arguments go out go around and talk to other people who went to doctors to doctors in your family and ask them about these practices so a quick guide to this course year one you will be introduced to the basic concepts of professionalism and ethics in year two we will focus on doctors as scholars and passionate practitioners of medicine the doctor-patient relationship and how you can carry yourself about as a physician the course will also skim over the concepts of patient safety in year three more confidentiality and autonomy are going to take the spotlight in the first term and in the second term the course will highlight the role of a doctor within the team how to deal with people in your medical team and in years four and five we are going to take more practical skills such as crisis management allocating resources medical legal aspects healthcare systems and quality medicine this year this is the lecture plan for this year this lecture is the definition of professionalism and overview of the subject the next lecture we are going to take an overview of medical ethics then we are going to examine the attributes of a physician and how a physician what qualities should be present in a physician and finally how to resolve ethical issues as they arise in medical practice then we are going to discuss the relation between empathy and clinical excellence doctor-patient relationship maintaining a professional boundary with your patient and sympathy and how you can take care of yourself against being involved with patients the assessment at the end of the year is going to have to be 50 marks on a written exam and 10 marks on an assignment for the time being our source for good medical practice is going to be the gmc website i have included the link in the slides as you can see please copy it into your browser have a look over this source and we will discuss it in the tutorial inshallah thank you very much for your attention in this lecture and hopefully uh i will see you soon in in the tutorial and we will meet in person and have a discussion over what was uh presented in the slides today thank you and welcome to medicine
